newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares to consolidate before fresh gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares to consolidate before fresh gains.

text.p: German shares are likely to consolidate around current record high levels before the DAX index makes a bid to break the psychologically important 4,000-point level in the coming weeks, traders said on Friday.
The DAX kept up its record-setting pace on Friday, climbing nearly 1.5 percent due to overnight Wall Street gains and a German insurance industry merger that fueled fresh demand.
The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade up 55.14 points, or 1.42 percent, to 3,942.53 points. The DAX had reached a new record high of 3,945.68 points at the outset of floor trade.
The advance was the latest in a string of gains in the DAX index, which ended bourse trade last Friday at 3,795 points.
Although the DAX was within sight of 4,000 points, some traders said the market needed to take a breather.
Future gains will also depend on the direction of the U.S. share market, which was closed Friday for a national holiday.

Shares in reinsurer Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG rose 485 marks to 5,336 marks after it said it would merge its Hamburg-Mannheimer AG unit with Victoria Holding AG, creating the second largest primary insurance company in Germany.
The news sparked hopes of further merger activity in the German insurance sector, giving Allianz AG a boost of 27.70 marks to 396.20 marks.

German utility giant RWE AG rose 70 pfennigs to 77.40 marks after announcing 1996/97 group net profit rose seven percent to just under 1.3 billion marks and sales up to 70.8 billion marks from 65.4 billion marks.
Carmakers were weaker after recent gains. BMW AG fell 15 marks to 1,460 marks. Volkswagen AG, Europe's largest carmaker, ended down 11.50 marks to 1,390.50 marks.
